brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Strong radial composition with concentric rings reads as breathing aura, supporting the organism metaphor at a glance
Clean metric tiles with consistent label/value hierarchy give scannable secondary data without cluttering the central viz
Dark palette plus single neon green accent feels coherent and lets the rings carry the visual weight
dominant_weaknesses: 3D emoji glyphs (brain, floppy disk) collide tonally with the otherwise techy neon vector aesthetic — feels like placeholder art
Both organisms show identical green rings and 'HEALTHY' state, so the core breathe-vs-pulse differentiation isn't visible in this static frame
Status panel top-right uses tiny cramped type and floats without alignment to the grid, weakening native polish
fix_priorities: Replace emoji centers with custom organic shapes that visibly deform with load — the metaphor depends on it
Differentiate ring color/cadence per state (calm green slow, amber medium, red fast) so stress is legible without motion
Re-align and re-type the status HUD to match the metric tile system for consistent rhythm
Tighten typographic scale: numbers feel oversized vs labels, creating uneven density across tiles
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral leads via the glowing rings, but behavioral clarity is weak (no urgency cues) and reflective payoff is thin since both organisms look identical.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the breathing-ring metaphor is established, but without state differentiation or motion-implying cues the 'organism' concept reads as decoration rather than diagnostic.
